title: Claude Certified Architect – Foundations (CCAR-F): Five Original Practice Exams
note: Original practice questions based on the published curriculum and documentation; not official exam items.

questions.question: Which instruction location is appropriate for a project-wide build command that every Claude Code session should know?

options.text: A personal skill
A one-time terminal message
A project CLAUDE.md
A path-scoped rule for one file extension

questions.explanation: Project CLAUDE.md is shared and loaded for sessions in the project, making it suitable for universal project facts.

questions.question: A research agent returns claims with source URLs, but the coordinator sends only claim text to a writer subagent. The final report lacks citations. What should change?

options.text: Move source URLs to a separate log the writer cannot read.
Increase the writer's output-token limit.
Pass each claim together with its source metadata to the writer.
Give the writer a stronger instruction to invent citations.

questions.explanation: Source attribution depends on preserving the link between each finding and its provenance during handoff.

questions.question: A customer says, 'Please connect me with a person.' The agent knows the answer to the billing question. What should it do?

options.text: Answer first and offer transfer only if rejected
Transfer to a human promptly
Ask the customer to justify the request
Use a sentiment score to decide

questions.explanation: An explicit human request is an escalation trigger regardless of whether the agent could resolve the issue.

questions.question: A service must show a policy summary while a customer waits on the phone; an overnight job analyzes thousands of old policies. Which allocation fits Message Batches?

options.text: Batch both tasks.
Use synchronous Messages for the live summary and Message Batches for the overnight analysis.
Avoid batch because it cannot process independent requests.
Use Message Batches for the live summary and synchronous Messages overnight.

questions.explanation: Batches are asynchronous and fit latency-tolerant work; a blocking live interaction needs a synchronous response.

questions.question: A CI runner launches Claude Code without a terminal for input. Which invocation is designed to process a prompt and exit?

options.text: claude --continue
claude -p 'Review the diff'
claude 'Review the diff'
claude /plan

questions.explanation: The -p or --print flag runs Claude Code non-interactively, prints the result, and exits.

questions.question: An agent must prevent deletion of a production database. At which point should a hook intervene?

options.text: Only when the session ends.
At final-answer formatting.
PostToolUse, after the deletion result returns.
PreToolUse, before the destructive tool runs.

questions.explanation: PreToolUse can deny a tool call before its side effect occurs.

questions.question: An application needs Claude's final response as a schema-conformant JSON object, without treating the data as a tool call. Which current API feature fits?

options.text: JSON outputs through output_config.format.
A larger context window.
A Message Batch custom_id.
Plain-text instructions saying to output JSON.

questions.explanation: JSON outputs constrain the response itself to a schema; strict tool use instead constrains tool inputs.

questions.question: A document pipeline always extracts fields, checks them, then writes a summary. Which design provides the clearest control flow?

options.text: Concurrent voting on every sentence.
Prompt chaining through the known stages.
An unrestricted agent with all tools.
Dynamic task planning at each document.

questions.explanation: Known sequential stages fit prompt chaining.

questions.question: A customer asks to replace a damaged item, change a delivery address, and check warranty coverage. What should the coordinator do?

options.text: Escalate immediately because the request has three parts.
Answer only the first request and wait.
Decompose the concerns, investigate relevant parts, and give a unified response.
Start three unrelated conversations without account context.

questions.explanation: A compound request requires coverage of each concern and one coherent resolution.

questions.question: A support system classifies requests as billing, account access, or technical issues and sends each to a specialized process. Which pattern is this?

options.text: Evaluator-optimizer.
Prompt chaining.
Routing.
Voting.

questions.explanation: Routing selects a specialized downstream process based on the input category.

questions.question: A source contract contains no renewal date, yet the extraction schema requires one. Which design avoids pressuring Claude to invent a date?

options.text: Repeat the extraction until a date appears.
Ask Claude to estimate a likely date.
Use a higher temperature.
Make the field nullable or optional and return null when absent.

questions.explanation: An absent source value cannot be recovered by retrying; the schema should allow missing information to be represented honestly.

questions.question: An agent chooses get_customer for an order-status request because get_customer and lookup_order both have vague descriptions. What should the architect improve first?

options.text: Make their descriptions distinguish purpose, inputs, and boundaries
Remove the order tool
Add a routing classifier before each call
Increase the model's context window

questions.explanation: Clear tool descriptions are the model's main guide for choosing between similar tools.

questions.question: Invoice extraction is 97% accurate overall, but handwritten receipts are rare. Before automating them, what should the team inspect?

options.text: The model's stated confidence alone
Accuracy by document type and extracted field
The number of input tokens per receipt
Only aggregate accuracy

questions.explanation: A high volume of easy documents can hide weak performance on a small, important segment.

questions.question: A document summarizer follows detailed format instructions but alternates between prose and tables across runs. What is the best first prompt change?

options.text: Add a few representative input-output examples in the desired format.
Ask for a confidence score before each paragraph.
Append the format instruction ten times.
Raise the temperature.

questions.explanation: Relevant examples demonstrate the exact target format and improve consistency more directly than repeated prose instructions.

questions.question: A review agent gives detailed feedback on early files but shallow feedback on later files. What is the best structural fix?

options.text: Stop after the first five files.
Repeat the instruction to be thorough several times.
Increase the maximum number of files in one prompt.
Review each file in a focused pass, then run a cross-file integration pass.

questions.explanation: Focused local passes reduce attention dilution; an integration pass catches cross-file issues.

questions.question: A team shares .mcp.json but each developer has a different API token. What should the file contain?

options.text: A shared personal token committed to git
A copy of each developer's secrets
No authentication mechanism
An environment-variable reference rather than a literal token

questions.explanation: Environment-variable expansion lets a shared configuration use local credentials without committing their values.

questions.question: A claims assistant summarizes each completed turn. Later it forgets an exact deductible and policy number. Which design most directly protects those facts?

options.text: Ask the model to reconstruct the missing numbers
Remove all earlier turns after summarization
Keep a structured case-facts record and carry it into later requests
Increase the model temperature

questions.explanation: Critical identifiers and amounts should be stored separately from lossy narrative summaries and supplied when needed.

questions.question: A synthesis subagent is asked to write a market brief, but the parent never includes the research subagent's findings in its prompt. What is the most likely failure?

options.text: The research agent's tools become available to the synthesis agent.
The synthesis agent can recover the findings from shared memory.
The Agent SDK automatically replays every parent tool result to it.
The synthesis agent lacks those findings because its context is separate.

questions.explanation: A subagent starts with isolated context and needs relevant prior findings passed explicitly.

questions.question: An agent is investigating why an unfamiliar service intermittently fails, and each clue may change the next diagnostic step. Which approach fits?

options.text: A fixed sequence that never changes.
A single response without tools.
Adaptive decomposition that revises the plan as evidence arrives.
A routing classifier only.

questions.explanation: Unknown root causes require a plan that can respond to new findings.

questions.question: A team wants Claude to label code-review findings as critical, major, or minor consistently. What should the prompt include?

options.text: Only dictionary definitions of the three words.
Representative code examples with the expected severity and a brief rationale.
A command to choose critical whenever uncertain.
The team's preferred temperature setting.

questions.explanation: Concrete labeled examples anchor each severity level and clarify the intended boundary between categories.

questions.question: A nightly batch returns results in an order different from submission order. How should the application match each result to its source record?

options.text: Compare the text length.
Use each request's unique custom_id.
Rely on the array position.
Sort by token usage.

questions.explanation: custom_id is the caller-supplied correlation key for matching individual batch results to requests.

questions.question: A prior session analyzed configuration files that were substantially rewritten overnight. The agent now cites removed settings. What is the best recovery?

options.text: Fork the stale history.
Resume again without mentioning the changes.
Ask the model to ignore all tool results while retaining them.
Start fresh with a structured summary and re-read changed files.

questions.explanation: A fresh session avoids stale tool results while a curated summary preserves still-valid findings.

questions.question: A single review of a 20-file pull request is deep on the first files and shallow on the rest. What workflow best addresses this?

options.text: Review only the first five files.
Review each file in a focused pass, then perform a separate cross-file integration pass.
Replace review with a confidence score from one pass.
Increase the context window only.

questions.explanation: Focused local passes give each file attention; an integration pass then checks interactions and inconsistencies across files.

questions.question: In a Claude Code session where Grep and Glob are available, a developer needs all files named *.test.tsx. Which tool matches file paths by pattern?

options.text: Grep
Glob
Read
Bash only

questions.explanation: Glob locates files by path or filename pattern.

questions.question: A request supplies an extraction tool with the default tool_choice of auto. What behavior must the caller allow for?

options.text: Claude always calls the extraction tool.
The API rejects all text responses.
Claude calls every available tool in order.
Claude may respond in text without calling a tool.

questions.explanation: With auto, Claude decides whether a tool call is needed, so a text-only response remains possible.

questions.question: One Messages API response contains two tool_use blocks with different IDs. How should the application continue?

options.text: Treat the presence of two blocks as end_turn.
Run both calls and return a tool_result matched to each tool_use ID.
Execute only the first block and discard the second.
Merge both calls into one new tool ID.

questions.explanation: Each client-tool request needs its own result paired by tool_use_id.

questions.question: A payment agent must verify account ownership before sending funds. Which control best guarantees the order?

options.text: A programmatic gate that rejects send_funds until verification succeeds.
Several examples of correct behavior.
A post-payment audit only.
A reminder in the user prompt.

questions.explanation: A prerequisite gate blocks the sensitive tool before execution if verification has not succeeded.

questions.question: A CI script uses --output-format json and --json-schema. Where should it read the schema-conforming result?

options.text: The top-level usage field
The stderr stream only
The first line of the text result
The structured_output field in the JSON envelope

questions.explanation: The JSON envelope contains metadata; the validated final value appears under structured_output.

questions.question: An invoice extractor succeeds on tables but misses amounts written in narrative paragraphs. Which examples should be added?

options.text: Only more clean tables.
Narrative and mixed-format invoices showing the correct extracted fields.
Examples with empty output for every narrative invoice.
Examples of unrelated document types.

questions.explanation: Few-shot examples should target the failing document structure, including how the value is extracted from narrative text.

questions.question: A server exposes a database schema as an MCP resource. Who determines how that resource enters model context?

options.text: The host application or client
The resource URI itself
Every tool call automatically
The schema's row count

questions.explanation: MCP resources are application-driven; the host decides how to present or attach them.

questions.question: A refund tool rejects a technically valid request because it exceeds a policy limit. What should the agent do?

options.text: Retry the same request immediately
Silently mark the refund complete
Follow the stated escalation or alternate workflow
Treat it as a network timeout

questions.explanation: A business-rule failure is not repaired by resending identical arguments; recovery needs another authorized path.

questions.question: After a long repository investigation, an assistant forgets the specific dependency path it found earlier. Which practice best preserves it?

options.text: Read every file again at each turn
Rely on a larger context window alone
Replace the dependency path with a generic design pattern
Save precise findings and file paths in a durable scratchpad

questions.explanation: A scratchpad externalizes precise findings so they can be retrieved after context fills with other outputs.

questions.question: A synthesis agent paraphrases subagent findings and loses their citations. What should subagents provide?

options.text: Structured findings with claim-to-source mappings that the synthesizer must preserve
Confidence labels with no URLs
Only source titles, without claims
A single unstructured narrative

questions.explanation: Explicit provenance must travel with each claim through synthesis and appear in the final answer.

questions.question: An extracted invoice has valid JSON, but its line items total 430 while the stated total is 480; the original document is available. What is the best next step?

options.text: Retry with only the phrase try again.
Accept it because the JSON schema passed.
Retry with the original invoice, the failed extraction, and the specific discrepancy.
Delete the stated total field.

questions.explanation: A semantic validator should detect the mismatch and give Claude precise feedback plus the source and prior output for correction.

questions.question: Claude generates a function and is then asked in the same conversation to review it. Subtle bugs keep passing review. What is the strongest architectural change?

options.text: Raise the output token limit for generation.
Ask the same conversation to review more carefully.
Use a fresh review invocation that sees the code but not the generation history.
Remove all tests before review.

questions.explanation: An independent reviewer lacks the generating conversation's prior decisions and can assess the artifact afresh.

questions.question: In a Claude Code session where Grep and Glob are available, a developer needs to find every file that calls processOrder. Which tool searches file contents?

options.text: Write
Grep
Glob
Edit

questions.explanation: Grep searches text inside files; a caller name is content, not a path pattern.

questions.question: Unit tests are co-located with source files across dozens of folders. The same test conventions should load only when a test file is used. What is the best configuration?

options.text: Put every test rule in root CLAUDE.md
Copy CLAUDE.md into every folder
Use .claude/rules/ with a paths glob for test files
Create a skill developers must invoke manually

questions.explanation: A path-scoped rule applies to matching files across directories without loading irrelevant conventions for other files.

questions.question: Claude Code keeps applying a known API migration inconsistently despite a prose description. What should the developer provide next?

options.text: Several exact before-and-after examples
A higher turn limit
A longer abstract description
Only the file tree

questions.explanation: Concrete input/output examples communicate the intended transformation more precisely than repeated prose.

questions.question: A codebase-analysis skill produces extensive file listings that should not fill the main conversation. Which frontmatter setting addresses this?

options.text: model: inherit
argument-hint: files
context: fork
paths: all

questions.explanation: context: fork runs the skill in an isolated subagent context and returns its result to the parent.

questions.question: A tool requires an order_id but sometimes receives no identifier. Which part of its definition should mark that field mandatory?

options.text: The input schema's required array
The tool result's content
The server transport
A resource URI

questions.explanation: A JSON Schema required list identifies mandatory input properties.

questions.question: A multi-agent support system has separate billing and shipping roles. How should tools be allocated?

options.text: Give every specialist every available tool
Split tools across servers but expose all to every agent
Give each specialist only tools relevant to its role
Give no tools to specialists

questions.explanation: Role-scoped tool sets reduce irrelevant choices and limit unintended capabilities.

questions.question: A stock lookup reaches the tool handler but its upstream API times out. Which response best supports model recovery?

options.text: A tool result with isError: true and actionable retry guidance
A normal success result saying Operation failed
An empty resource list
A different tool name

questions.explanation: An execution failure belongs in a tool result marked isError so the model can see the cause and decide whether to retry.

questions.question: A team must block a dangerous shell command in every Claude Code session. Which mechanism provides an enforced control?

options.text: A permission deny rule in settings
An example in a skill description
A warning in CLAUDE.md
A reminder in the first prompt

questions.explanation: CLAUDE.md guides model behavior but is not an enforcement layer. A deny rule is evaluated by the client.

questions.question: A team wants to compare two migration strategies from the same completed analysis while preserving the original investigation. Which session action fits?

options.text: Start two blank sessions with no baseline.
Continue the original twice without branching.
Fork the session into independent branches.
Clear the session transcript.

questions.explanation: Forking gives each alternative the shared starting context and a separate continuation.

questions.question: A long research packet has critical findings buried among many source excerpts. The synthesizer repeatedly misses them. What should change first?

options.text: Repeat a generic instruction to read carefully
Put a concise key-findings summary first, then labeled detail sections
Delete all citations to shorten the packet
Increase the number of subagents

questions.explanation: Position and structure affect retrieval from long context; front-load key findings and keep detailed evidence organized.

questions.question: A travel assistant receives stop_reason "tool_use" with a client-tool request to check a train schedule. What should the application do next?

options.text: Ask Claude to repeat the same request without tools.
Start a new unrelated conversation with the tool output.
Return the assistant text as the final answer.
Execute the requested tool, append the assistant response and matching tool_result, then call Claude again.

questions.explanation: A client tool runs in the application; its result must be sent back before Claude can finish the turn.

questions.question: A code-review assistant reports many naming preferences as defects. Which system-prompt change most directly improves precision?

options.text: Tell it to be conservative.
Increase max_tokens so it can justify every finding.
Define reportable bug and security categories and explicitly exclude style preferences.
Ask it to report only findings above 90% self-reported confidence.

questions.explanation: Explicit inclusion and exclusion criteria give the model an actionable decision boundary; vague caution and raw confidence do not.

questions.question: Three inventory tools return dates in different formats. Which mechanism can normalize their returned data before Claude reads it?

options.text: A system prompt asking Claude to guess each format.
An iteration cap on the agent loop.
A PreToolUse hook that inspects tool arguments.
A PostToolUse hook that transforms tool output.

questions.explanation: PostToolUse receives the completed result and can standardize what the model sees.

questions.question: Two credible reports give different values for a market indicator and use different measurement periods. How should a synthesis report present them?

options.text: Show both values with source, period, and possible methodological differences
Omit the indicator entirely
Average the figures without qualification
Keep only the newer report

questions.explanation: Preserving both attributed values and their temporal context avoids false certainty.

questions.question: A research subagent times out after collecting two of three requested documents. What should it return to its coordinator?

options.text: The two findings plus the failure type, attempted query, and missing coverage
A fatal error with no documents
A fabricated summary of the third document
An empty successful result

questions.explanation: Structured partial failure preserves useful evidence and gives the coordinator a basis for retry or disclosure.

questions.question: A document-reading subagent only needs approved document URLs. Which interface best follows least privilege?

options.text: A tool that also changes permissions
A general shell command executor
An unrestricted fetch_url tool
A constrained load_document tool that validates URLs

questions.explanation: A constrained tool exposes the needed capability without broad arbitrary URL access.

questions.question: A developer paused an Agent SDK task yesterday; the repository has not changed. They need to continue the same investigation with its prior tool results. What should they use?

options.text: Discard the prior history and rerun everything.
Resume the specific prior session.
Fork into two independent branches.
A completely fresh session.

questions.explanation: Resume restores the prior conversation when that context remains valid.

questions.question: A payment integration has three viable architectures and affects several services. How should Claude Code begin?

options.text: Directly edit the first service
Run /compact before reading code
Create a global skill for the integration
Enter plan mode and compare approaches before edits

questions.explanation: Plan mode is suited to ambiguous, multi-file architectural work that needs exploration before implementation.

questions.question: Two developers need the same MCP server configuration when they clone a project. Where should it be stored?

options.text: In the model's auto memory
Only in one developer's ~/.claude.json
.mcp.json at the project root, committed to version control
In a private chat message

questions.explanation: Claude Code project-scoped MCP servers are configured in the repository's .mcp.json.

questions.question: A team knows every step of invoice extraction in advance and needs predictable execution. Which architecture fits best?

options.text: An open-ended agent that invents steps on every invoice.
A tool-use loop with no stopping condition.
A group of agents that always debate every field.
A predefined workflow with fixed steps.

questions.explanation: A workflow is appropriate when the code path is known and consistency matters.

questions.question: A new engineer clones a repository but Claude Code does not follow the team's naming standard. The standard exists only in the lead engineer's home directory. Where should it go?

options.text: The repository's CLAUDE.md or .claude/CLAUDE.md
A global MCP server configuration
The new engineer's ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md only
A prompt pasted into every session

questions.explanation: Project instructions are version-controlled and shared with the team; user instructions in a home directory are personal.

questions.question: A data conversion must preserve nulls, handle empty arrays, and satisfy a schema. What gives Claude Code the clearest iterative feedback?

options.text: A personal preference in settings
Failing tests covering the specified cases
A command to compact context
An open-ended request to improve quality

questions.explanation: Tests make expected behavior and edge cases observable through pass/fail results.

questions.question: A stack trace identifies a one-line condition that must change in one function. The fix and location are known. Which workflow is most efficient?

options.text: Use direct execution, then run the relevant check
Start with a broad architecture plan
Fork a research skill
Rewrite the entire module

questions.explanation: A clear, limited edit does not need a separate planning phase, but it should still be verified.

questions.question: A support tool returns forty fields, but the task needs only order ID, status, and amount. What should the application do before the next model turn?

options.text: Trim the tool result to relevant fields while retaining necessary identifiers
Pass all fields in case they become useful
Repeat the same tool call
Convert the result to a longer prose paragraph

questions.explanation: Filtering irrelevant tool output reduces context use while retaining facts required for the task.

questions.question: A repository needs a reusable /release-check workflow with supporting checklists. Which path fits the Skills system?

options.text: .claude/skills/release-check.md
.claude/rules/release-check.json
~/.claude/CLAUDE.md
.claude/skills/release-check/SKILL.md

questions.explanation: A project skill is a directory containing SKILL.md; supporting files can sit alongside it.

questions.question: Two subagents can independently inspect a contract and a financial spreadsheet. Which invocation strategy reduces elapsed time?

options.text: Merge both tasks into one vague prompt.
Have the agents edit each other's prompts directly.
Start both subagents concurrently and aggregate their results afterward.
Run the contract agent, then wait before starting the spreadsheet agent.

questions.explanation: Independent subtasks can run in parallel before the parent combines their outputs.

questions.question: A server-tool turn ends with stop_reason "pause_turn". What is the correct interpretation?

options.text: A client tool must be run locally.
The server-side turn is paused and should be continued with the prior response.
The task has completed normally.
The model refused the request.

questions.explanation: pause_turn means the long-running server-tool loop needs a continuation, not a final answer.

questions.question: A coordinator needs to inspect tests, payment code, and deployment configuration. Why delegate each investigation to a focused subagent?

options.text: They can share hidden context automatically
Subagents always use fewer tokens overall
Subagents eliminate the need to validate results
Their separate contexts keep verbose exploration from crowding the coordinator's context

questions.explanation: Focused subagents can explore independently and return compact findings to the coordinator.

questions.question: An expense receipt may omit a purchase-order number. How should the extraction schema represent that field?

options.text: Allow null or make the field optional when it is absent.
Require a nonempty string for every receipt.
Replace it with the vendor name.
Use an enum containing only known purchase-order numbers.

questions.explanation: Allowing a missing value helps the model report absent information without inventing a plausible identifier.

questions.question: With Grep available in Claude Code, a developer starts from an error message and wants to understand only relevant code. Which exploration sequence conserves context?

options.text: Grep the message, then Read the relevant files and follow imports
Glob only directories and stop
Write a new file first
Read every file before searching

questions.explanation: Narrow search before reading avoids loading unrelated files into context.

questions.question: Claude returns a text block saying it will check a record and also returns a tool_use block. What should control the loop?

options.text: The response stop_reason, which indicates a tool call is pending.
Whether the sentence contains the word "check".
The first content block being text.
A fixed two-iteration limit.

questions.explanation: Text can accompany a tool call; stop_reason identifies why the response stopped.

questions.question: A prompt includes five examples, all with the same document layout. Production documents vary widely. What improvement best supports generalization?

options.text: Use diverse examples covering the important layouts and edge cases.
Remove every example.
Increase the number of copies of the existing layout.
Force the model to use one layout for all source documents.

questions.explanation: Relevant, diverse examples reduce unintended pattern matching and cover the real variation seen in production.

questions.question: A tool result says access denied because the caller lacks a required role. What recovery is appropriate?

options.text: Ask for authorized access or escalate
Remove the error flag
Invent a result
Retry the same credentials indefinitely

questions.explanation: A permission failure requires appropriate authorization or escalation, not a blind retry.

questions.question: A drafting agent creates a proposal; a second agent checks it against an explicit rubric and returns targeted feedback for revision. Which pattern is this?

options.text: Routing.
Tool search.
Evaluator-optimizer.
Prompt caching.

questions.explanation: The evaluator checks an output against criteria and feeds a revision loop.

questions.question: A style guide prefers title case headings, and an occasional inconsistency has little consequence. Which control is proportionate?

options.text: Block every response with a pre-execution hook.
Require human approval for every heading.
Prompt guidance describing the preferred style.
Disable all model-generated headings.

questions.explanation: Low-stakes preferences can be expressed through prompts; deterministic gates are for requirements that must never be skipped.

questions.question: A team proposes Message Batches solely to reduce cost for an interactive checkout assistant. What is the central objection?

options.text: Batch cannot use vision inputs.
Batch has asynchronous completion and no immediate-response latency guarantee.
Batch results are always in submission order.
Batch does not accept system messages.

questions.explanation: The cost discount is useful only when the workflow can tolerate delayed completion.

questions.question: An agent has many near-identical transformation tools that all accept data and an operation. What can reduce selection complexity without removing capability?

options.text: A parameterized transform tool with an operation enum
A separate MCP server for each transform while exposing all
Longer names for all transforms only
Giving every transform to every subagent

questions.explanation: Related operations with a common shape can be consolidated under one well-defined parameterized interface.

questions.question: A team splits a 400-line CLAUDE.md into files imported with @ paths. What changes about context use when the parent file loads?

options.text: Imports are inlined, so their content still consumes context
Only one imported file is loaded at a time
Imports are stored outside the model context
Imports turn instructions into enforced permissions

questions.explanation: Imports improve organization but load alongside the parent; path-scoped rules are a better way to avoid irrelevant context.

questions.question: A single analyze_document tool extracts fields, summarizes text, and verifies claims, and Claude often chooses the wrong behavior. What interface change is most direct?

options.text: Split it into purpose-specific tools with clear contracts
Move the tool to another MCP server without changing it
Hide all output schemas
Use the same description for all operations

questions.explanation: Distinct jobs are easier to select when each has a clear name and input/output contract.

questions.question: In an orchestrator-workers design, who should decide which workers to invoke and combine their outputs?

options.text: Every worker independently, without coordination.
The first worker that finishes.
The end user after each tool call.
The orchestrator.

questions.explanation: The orchestrator dynamically decomposes the task, delegates work, and synthesizes results.

questions.question: An application must resume a specific older SDK conversation rather than whichever session ran most recently. What should it retain?

options.text: The number of tool calls.
Only the latest answer text.
Only the model name.
The session ID and pass it to resume.

questions.explanation: A specific prior conversation is identified by its session ID.

questions.question: A team has a deployment checklist needed only on release days. Where should it live?

options.text: Root CLAUDE.md for every session
A project skill invoked for releases
A user-only CLAUDE.md
A path rule matching every file

questions.explanation: A task-specific workflow belongs in an on-demand skill rather than universal instructions.

questions.question: A team puts errorCategory and isRetryable in structuredContent of an MCP tool error result. How should those fields be understood?

options.text: Transport negotiation headers
A replacement for isError
Application-level conventions, not universal MCP protocol fields
Mandatory JSON-RPC envelope fields

questions.explanation: MCP defines isError and result content; category and retry metadata can be useful application-defined structure.

questions.question: A model emits a confidence score for each review finding. Before automatic routing based on a threshold, what evidence is needed?

options.text: A promise in the prompt that confidence is calibrated.
A labeled validation set showing how the scores relate to actual correctness.
A larger context window.
One successful demonstration.

questions.explanation: Self-reported confidence should be calibrated empirically against known outcomes before it controls routing decisions.

questions.question: A developer wants an MCP server available only in the current project and not shared with teammates. Which Claude Code scope fits?

options.text: Managed organization
Project
Local
User

questions.explanation: Local scope applies to the current project but is personal; project scope is shared through .mcp.json.

questions.question: A rule in .claude/rules/api.md declares paths for src/api/**/*.ts. When should its instructions apply?

options.text: Every session regardless of work
Only when Claude works with matching files
Only after /api is typed
Only after a CI job runs

questions.explanation: The paths frontmatter conditionally loads rule guidance for matching files.

questions.question: A research pipeline must support audit of each final claim. Which subagent output is most useful?

options.text: Claim plus source URL, document title, supporting location or excerpt, and date
Claim plus the subagent's self-rated confidence only
A ranked list of URLs without extracted claims
A prose summary with references removed

questions.explanation: Structured claim-source mappings let downstream stages verify and retain attribution.
